text:
Predicates:
Champion(x) ::: x is a Grand Slam champion.
Actor(x) ::: x is an Oscar-nominated actor.
TennisPlayer(x) ::: x is a professional tennis player.
Celebrity(x) ::: x is a celebrity.
Athlete(x) ::: x is an athlete.
WellPaid(x) ::: x is well paid.
Famous(x) ::: x is famous.
LiveInTaxHaven(x) ::: x lives in a tax haven.
Premises:
∀x (Champion(x) ∨ Actor(x)) ::: A person is either a Grand Slam champion or an Oscar-nominated actor.
∀x (Champion(x) → TennisPlayer(x)) ::: All people who are Grand Slam champions are professional tennis players.
∀x (Actor(x) → Celebrity(x)) ::: All Oscar-nominated actors are celebrities.
∀x (TennisPlayer(x) → Athlete(x)) ::: All professional tennis players are athletes.
∀x (Celebrity(x) → WellPaid(x)) ::: If a person is a celebrity then they are well paid.
∀x (Athlete(x) → Famous(x)) ::: If a person is an athlete then they are famous.
∀x (WellPaid(x) → LiveInTaxHaven(x)) ::: All well-paid people live in tax havens.
(Famous(djokovic) ∧ Athlete(djokovic)) → LiveInTaxHaven(djokovic) ::: If Djokovic is famous and is an athlete, then Djokovic lives in well paid.
Conclusion:
¬LiveInTaxHaven(djokovic) ::: Djokovic does not live in a tax haven.
